report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a domain/content shift — Model B (B − A positive) is biased toward culinary / restaurant / food-blog style continuations (words like restaurant, cooking, Chef, baking, Cake, blogs, Blog, Cooking, magazine, Chef) especially at early-following token positions (pos1–pos4) in later layers. In other words, compared with A, B more strongly activates tokens associated with food/restaurant/recipe/blogging content.

Why I believe this
- Layer/position concentration: the difference norm is very large in later layers (layers ~16–25) and is especially concentrated at positions 1–4 (pos1 has the biggest peaks). That pattern is consistent with a high-level, late-layer preference for certain continuation genres rather than a low-level tokenization effect.
- Logit-lens alignment: many of the highest-norm (layer,position) cells point toward culinary/publication tokens: “restaurant”, “Restaurant”, “cooking”, “Cooking”, “Chef”, “baking”, “blogs”, “blog”, “Cake”, “professional”, “Magazine”, “Made”, “Hot”, etc., repeatedly across layers 16–25 and across pos2–pos4. That is a coherent semantic cluster (food/recipes/restaurants and blogging/magazine language).
- Secondary signals: earlier/intermediate-layer pos0 cells show other tokens (Me, corporations, revenue, metropolitan, chiropractic, billionaire, doctoral, Touch, Michele/Weller) but these are less consistent across many high-norm cells. The dominant, repeated theme in the high-norm late-layer pos1–4 cells is the culinary/blogging cluster.

Caveats
- Patchscope readouts were not provided (or are empty in the evidence), so I can’t show actual generated continuations to confirm the logit-lens prediction in free-text continuations.
- I can name the apparent domain bias (food/restaurant/blogging) but cannot infer a specific training objective or exact dataset difference (only that B favors those tokens/continuations relative to A).
